input.quote: 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.
input.rationale: Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created and paid for by us and leaves us only a revocable, non-transferable, term-limited licence. That fails the fallback as well as the preferred position: the Deliverable licence is neither perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide nor sublicensable (Section 13.2's perpetual paid-up licence reaches only Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable, not the Deliverable itself), so on expiry our right to use work product created specifically for us simply ends. The rest of the IP section is already at the preferred position: Section 14.1 leaves us all Customer Data and our independent IP with Vendor holding only a limited processing right to provide the Services for us (reinforced by Section 15.1), Section 14.3 retains Vendor's pre-existing Vendor Technology, Section 13.2 grants the perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor Technology, and Section 14.4 creates no joint ownership. The shortest complete cure is therefore to flip Section 14.2 to Customer ownership with a Vendor assignment and drop the now-redundant revocable licence.

proposal.summary: Reverse Deliverable ownership to Customer with a Vendor assignment
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own what we pay for, so we have flipped Section 14.2 to give us ownership of Deliverables and work product created for us, with Vendor assigning that right, title, and interest; the revocable term-limited licence is no longer needed. Vendor's pre-existing Vendor Technology retention in Section 14.3 and the perpetual embedded licence in Section 13.2 are unchanged.
